svg.title: How a Customizable Contraction Hierarchy answers a shortest-path query
svg.desc: Left: the Italian road network, with each city drawn larger and darker the higher it sits in the hierarchy. The first separator, Caserta, Termoli and Campobasso, cuts Italy in two; dashed lines are the shortcuts added while contracting. Right: the elimination tree of the same hierarchy. A query from Roma to Palermo climbs the tree from both cities until the two climbs meet, then unpacks the shortcuts into the real route.
svg.text: How CCH answers Roma to Palermo: climb, meet, unpack
The hierarchy of the Italy sample: 212 roads become 424 arcs with the shortcuts; the tree is 28 levels deep.
